chapters.name: General Organic Chemistry (GOC) & Hydrocarbons
keyPoints: Carbocation Stability: Tropylium > Triphenylmethyl > Benzyl ≈ Allyl > 3° > 2° > 1° > CH3+ > Vinyl > Phenyl. (Rearrangements via 1,2-hydride and 1,2-methyl shifts occur to maximize stability).
Carbanion Stability: Aromatic > sp-C (≡C-) > 1° > 2° > 3°. Stabilized by -I, -M groups.
Free Radical Stability: Benzyl > Allyl > 3° > 2° > 1° > Methyl.
Aromaticity (Hückel's Rule): Planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with (4n + 2)π electrons is aromatic; 4n π electrons is anti-aromatic (highly unstable).
Electrophilic Addition of HX: Markovnikov's rule (proton adds to carbon with more H's via carbocation).
HBr with Peroxides (Kharasch Effect): Free radical mechanism yields Anti-Markovnikov product (operates strictly for HBr, not HCl or HI).
Ozonolysis of Alkenes: Reductive cleavage with O3 followed by Zn/H2O breaks C=C into aldehydes and ketones without over-oxidation.
Acidity of Alkynes: Terminal alkynes (HC≡CH, RC≡CH) are acidic due to 50% s-character of sp-carbon; react with Na or NaNH2 to liberate H2.
